name: Pierogies with Kielbasa and Fried Onions
summary: Frozen pierogies pan-fried with sliced kielbasa and a lot of onion. One pan, twenty-five minutes.
instructions: Boil the frozen pierogies in salted water for 4–5 minutes until they float. Drain well.
While they boil, melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden. Move them to a plate.
Add the kielbasa to the same pan and fry 3–4 minutes until browned. Move it to the plate with the onions.
Melt the remaining butter in the pan. Fry the pierogies in one layer, 2–3 minutes per side, until golden. Work in two batches if needed.
Return the onions and kielbasa to the pan, toss together, and season with pepper. Serve with sour cream.

substitutions.substitute: 1 kg russet potatoes, cubed, par-boiled 8 minutes, then pan-fried the same way with a handful of cheddar
substitutions.costNote: Potatoes cost about $0.66, bringing the total to roughly $7.30. Gluten-free frozen pierogies are about $9 and push it over $15.

glutenFree.notes: Most smoked kielbasa is gluten-free, but some brands use wheat fillers. Check the label.

budgetNotes: Great Value potato, bacon and onion pierogies ($2.73) are cheaper than Cheemo and work the same way.
Skip the kielbasa for a vegetarian version at about $6.90. Add a second bag of pierogies if you need more food.
Boiling first and then frying keeps the pierogies from splitting in the pan.
